reading.title: The History of Medicine
reading.text: Medicine has evolved from ancient herbal remedies to modern gene therapy. The Code of Hammurabi, written around 1754 BCE, contains some of the earliest medical regulations. Hippocrates, the 'Father of Medicine,' established the Hippocratic Oath around 400 BCE, emphasizing ethical practice. The Middle Ages saw the rise of hospitals, while the 19th century introduced anesthesia and antiseptics. Alexander Fleming's discovery of penicillin in 1928 marked the beginning of modern antibiotics. Today, mRNA vaccines and CRISPR gene editing represent the cutting edge of medical science.

reading.title: Urban Farming: Growing Food in the City
reading.text: As the world's population grows and cities expand, traditional agriculture struggles to meet food demand. Urban farming, the practice of growing food within cities, has emerged as a sustainable solution. Rooftop gardens, vertical farms in warehouses, and community plots in vacant lots are becoming common. These farms reduce the distance food travels, cutting carbon emissions, and they provide fresh produce to communities that may lack grocery stores. Hydroponic and aeroponic systems allow crops to be grown without soil, using 90% less water than traditional farming. Many cities now support urban farming through grants and legal protections.

reading.title: Renewable Energy and the Future
reading.text: The transition to renewable energy is critical for combating climate change. Solar and wind power are the fastest-growing sources, with global capacity doubling every few years. However, renewable energy faces challenges: solar panels produce power only during the day, and wind turbines work only when the wind blows. Battery storage technology is improving rapidly, allowing excess energy to be stored for later use. Some countries like Iceland and Norway already generate nearly 100% of their electricity from renewable sources. The key to a sustainable future will be combining multiple renewable sources with smart grid technology to ensure reliable supply.
